headline: Macro favors Capital (Labor Share 93.7, Profits/Wages +7.5%); Equities show 3M pullback in AI hardware (-22.73%) vs. IT/Staffing bounce (-5.69%)

bullets.title: Labor Share Compression
bullets.text: BLS Nonfarm Labor Share stands at 93.73 (-0.67% QoQ, -1.60% YoY), remaining structurally below the 2017=100 baseline.
bullets.reason: Real output growth is accruing to capital owners faster than compensation: nonfarm payrolls sit at 159.3M with average weekly hours capped at 34.4h and hourly earnings at $38.00/hr.

bullets.title: Profits Outpacing Wages
bullets.text: Corporate Profits-to-Wage-Bill ratio hit 0.414 (+2.56% QoQ, +18.65% YoY).
bullets.reason: BEA Corporate Profits expanded to $4,419.0B SAAR (+3.25% QoQ, +23.08% YoY) while the annualized private wage bill grew only +0.47% MoM (+4.30% YoY) to $10,827.8B.

bullets.title: Watchlist Spread Drivers
bullets.text: 3M Watchlist Spread is -17.03pp (Capital Enablers -22.73% vs. Labor-Heavy -5.69%).
bullets.reason: Short-term multiple compression hit AI hardware/power names (SMCI (-39.4%), VRT (-35.6%), NVDA (-34.4%)), while oversold IT outsourcers & staffing rebounded (EPAM (+46.0%), INFY (+9.4%), CTSH (-0.2%)). Over 1Y, hardware/grid winners (ANET (+31.1%), PWR (+25.7%), GEV (+25.2%)) still anchor the capex cycle.

bullets.title: AI & Power Capex Catalyst
bullets.reason: Physical power & cooling bottleneck driving HALO infrastructure capex. Also tracked: "KT Cloud signs 60MW lease at data center in Ansan, South Korea" (Data Center Dynamics).

bullets.title: Workforce & Macro Signal
bullets.text: "An AI apprenticeship programme seeks to empower international agency staff amid job cuts" (Geneva Solutions) — with U.S. unemployment at 4.1% (2026-10-01).
bullets.reason: Direct headcount reduction / AI substitution compressing labor share.
